title: Connect & Disconnect a Cluster with castctl CLI | Connecting Your Cluster | Cast AI Docs
markdown:
For AI agents: the docs index is at https://docs.cast.ai/llms.txt. Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version.

`castctl` is the recommended way to connect Kubernetes clusters to Cast AI. It auto-detects your cloud provider, cluster name, and region from your kubeconfig, walks you through feature selection, and handles cluster registration, IAM setup, and the Helm install in a single command.

You can also connect clusters from the [Cast AI console](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-via-console) or with the [Terraform provider](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/terraform-provider).

## What castctl supports   [Skip link to What castctl supports](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#what-castctl-supports)

- **Cloud providers**: Amazon EKS, Google GKE, Microsoft AKS, and [Cast AI Anywhere](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/cast-ai-anywhere-overview) (on-premises, bare metal, and other clouds).
- **Features**: Cost Monitoring (always enabled), [Node Autoscaling](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/autoscaler), and [Workload Autoscaling](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/workload-autoscaling-overview).
- **Karpenter**: If Karpenter is already installed in the cluster, `castctl` offers to keep it as your node provisioner via [Cast AI for Karpenter](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/karpenter-enterprise).

> 📘
>
> ### Plan requirements   [Skip link to Plan requirements](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#plan-requirements)
>
> Node Autoscaling and Workload Autoscaling are Premium features. Cost Monitoring is available on every plan.

## Before you start   [Skip link to Before you start](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#before-you-start)

Before you connect a cluster with `castctl`, make sure you have:

- A Cast AI account ( [sign up](https://console.cast.ai/)).
- A Kubernetes cluster on EKS, GKE, AKS, or a [Cast AI Anywhere](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/cast-ai-anywhere-overview) supported environment.
- `kubectl` configured for that cluster with admin access (`kubectl auth can-i '*' '*'`).
- Cloud-side permissions equivalent to the console connection script's least-privileged policy. See [Cloud permissions](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/cloud-permissions).
- `metrics-server` installed in the cluster, if you plan to enable Workload Autoscaling.

`castctl` bundles its own Helm logic, so you do **not** need `helm`, `jq`, or `yq` installed locally.

## Install castctl   [Skip link to Install castctl](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#install-castctl)

Shell

```shell
brew tap castai/tap
brew trust --cask castai/tap/castctl
brew install castctl
```

To upgrade to the latest version:

Shell

```shell
brew update && brew upgrade castctl
```

Shell

```shell
curl -fsSL https://get.cast.ai/linux | bash
```

The script installs `castctl` to `~/.local/bin` by default and verifies the SHA256 checksum.

Pin a specific version or change the install location:

Shell

```shell
# Install to /usr/local/bin
curl -fsSL https://get.cast.ai/linux \
  | bash
```

PowerShell

```powershell
iwr -useb https://get.cast.ai/windows | iex
```

Verify the installation:

Shell

```shell
castctl version
```

## Log in   [Skip link to Log in](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#log-in)

Authenticate `castctl` with Cast AI using your browser:

1. Run the login command:



Shell





```shell
castctl auth login
```

2. `castctl` opens your default browser and asks to sign in to your Cast AI account.

3. After authentication, control returns to your terminal. If you belong to more than one organization, pick one from the interactive list. If you belong to a single organization, it's selected automatically.

4. `castctl` saves your token and organization ID to `~/.config/castctl/config.yaml` and prints a confirmation message.


> 📘
>
> ### Switching account or organization   [Skip link to Switching account or organization](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#switching-account-or-organization)
>
> Run `castctl auth login` again. It overwrites the stored credentials.

## Connect your cluster   [Skip link to Connect your cluster](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#connect-your-cluster)

1. Start the interactive connection:



Shell





```shell
castctl cluster connect
```





`castctl` detects the cloud provider, cluster name, and region from your kubeconfig and node labels, then prints the resolved configuration for you to review.

2. Select the features you want to enable.

3. Confirm the **Proceed with connecting?** prompt. `castctl` then:
1. Registers the cluster with Cast AI.
2. Installs the `castai` Helm chart in the `castai-agent` namespace.
3. Creates the IAM resources required in your cloud account (AWS / GCP / Azure).
4. On success, `castctl` prints the cluster's Cast AI console URL. Open it to verify everything is connected.


### Preview without making changes   [Skip link to Preview without making changes](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#preview-without-making-changes)

Resolve the configuration and print it as YAML without registering the cluster or modifying anything:

Shell

```shell
castctl cluster connect --dry-run
```

Useful for validating that auto-detection picked the right provider, region, and cluster name.

### Non-interactive mode (CI/scripts)   [Skip link to Non-interactive mode (CI/scripts)](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#non-interactive-mode-ciscripts)

In CI pipelines or scripts, disable prompts with `--non-interactive`. The process can be customized using flags passed to the binary.

Shell

```shell
castctl cluster connect \
  --non-interactive \
  --cluster-optimization=false \
  --workload-autoscaler=true
```

For the complete list of flags supported by the current `castctl`, including feature toggles, GKE credential method, and Helm values overrides, run:

Shell

```shell
castctl cluster connect --help
```

### Custom umbrella chart values   [Skip link to Custom umbrella chart values](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#custom-umbrella-chart-values)

During cluster onboarding, `castctl` installs the Cast AI components using an umbrella Helm chart. You can customize the chart values (such as tolerations, node selectors, or resource limits) by providing a YAML values file with the `--umbrella-values-file` flag:

Shell

```shell
castctl cluster connect --umbrella-values-file /path/to/custom-values.yaml
```

This flag accepts a YAML file containing Helm values that are merged with the configuration `castctl` generates based on your feature selections. This approach provides flexibility to configure values that `castctl` doesn't explicitly manage through command-line flags.

Example `custom-values.yaml`:

YAML

```yaml
global:
  tolerations:
    - key: "dedicated"
      operator: "Equal"
      value: "castai"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
```

For a complete reference of available values in the umbrella chart, see the [castai-umbrella Helm chart documentation](https://github.com/castai/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/castai-umbrella).

## Connect a Cast AI Anywhere cluster   [Skip link to Connect a Cast AI Anywhere cluster](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#connect-a-cast-ai-anywhere-cluster)

For clusters running outside EKS, GKE, or AKS, such as on-premises, bare metal, or other cloud providers, use the `--provider anywhere` flag:

Shell

```shell
castctl cluster connect --provider anywhere
```

Click here to learn more about [Cast AI Anywhere](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/cast-ai-anywhere-overview).

## After connecting   [Skip link to After connecting](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#after-connecting)

- **Import your existing node configuration.** This is the recommended way to prepare a newly-connected cluster: `castctl cluster import-config` discovers your existing node groups and creates matching node configurations and node templates automatically, so Cast AI provisions nodes that match what you already run. See [Import and apply cluster configuration with castctl](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/castctl-import-cluster-configuration).
- **Review the Node Autoscaler checklist.** Whether or not you import existing config, check the [Node Autoscaler preparation checklist](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/autoscaler-checklist) for the workload-level requirements (PodDisruptionBudgets, startup probes) automated import can't set for you.
- **Migrating from standalone Helm charts?** If the cluster was previously connected using individual Cast AI Helm releases, `castctl cluster migrate` consolidates them into the unified umbrella chart. This causes brief downtime: Node Autoscaling and Workload Autoscaling pause while the migration runs. See [Migrate standalone Helm charts with castctl](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/castctl-migrate-standalone-helm-charts). If those releases are managed by ArgoCD, Flux, or Terraform, see [Migrate GitOps and IaC installations with castctl](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/castctl-migrate-gitops) instead. It is a phased flow with no downtime.

For the complete list of castctl commands and flags, see the [castctl command reference](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/castctl-reference).

## Disconnect a cluster   [Skip link to Disconnect a cluster](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#disconnect-a-cluster)

> ⚠️
>
> ### This removes Cast AI completely   [Skip link to This removes Cast AI completely](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#this-removes-cast-ai-completely)
>
> `castctl cluster disconnect` performs the equivalent of both **Disconnect cluster** and **Remove cluster** in the Cast AI console: it uninstalls the Cast AI Helm releases, deletes the IAM resources created during the connection, and removes the cluster record from Cast AI.

> 🚧
>
> ### Not for Terraform-managed clusters   [Skip link to Not for Terraform-managed clusters](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/connect-with-castctl\#not-for-terraform-managed-clusters)
>
> Do **not** run `castctl cluster disconnect` against a cluster that was connected with the [Cast AI Terraform provider](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/terraform-provider). The CLI does not coordinate with Terraform state and will leave your Terraform configuration out of sync. For Terraform-managed clusters, run `terraform destroy` instead. See [Disconnect your cluster](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/disconnect-your-cluster#terraform-managed-clusters).
>
> Clusters connected via the Cast AI console or `castctl` are supported.

1. Switch your kubeconfig to the cluster you want to disconnect.

2. Run the disconnect command:



Shell





```shell
castctl cluster disconnect
```





`castctl` reads the Cast AI cluster ID from the in-cluster configuration, so you usually do not need to provide it.

3. Review the summary box. `castctl` prints every cloud resource it removed, any resources that were already absent, and any warnings to follow up on.


If a step fails, `castctl` prints a failure box noting which step failed and which cloud resources were already cleaned up. Fix the underlying issue and re-run the command. Partial progress is preserved.

For the full list of disconnect options (including flags to skip cloud cleanup or the Kubernetes uninstall), run:

Shell

```shell
castctl cluster disconnect --help
```
